item.title: Jalen Brunson drops final verdict on ‘performative’ Taylor Swift’s Knicks fandom debate after Tyler Kolek’s callout
item.description: Jalen Brunson drops final verdict on ‘performative’ Taylor Swift’s Knicks fandom debate after Tyler Kolek’s callout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The final word on the Taylor Swift “performative” New York Knicks fandom has been said by team captain Jalen Brunson , who was hoping to put out the fires. Speaking to Us Weekly, Brunson couldn’t believe he had to weigh in on the drama. However, the team captain was quick to defend Swift and say that she is “a member of the Knicks fandom.” “I can’t believe I have to say this,” he said. “But I didn’t say what was said. Being one of the leaders of the team — the captain of the team — I guess I now have to help somebody out. Yes, she’s a member of the Knicks fandom. Yes, she is.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Swift’s Knicks fandom has been called into question over the last few weeks. Broadcaster Monica McNutt was famously caught saying, “She’s not a Knicks fan. Get out of here, girl,” on the hot mics. Then, Tyler Kolek , one of Brunson’s teammates, called her fandom “performative.” He didn’t see her at many games, and he wasn’t sure if she was really a fan. “At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative ’cause they just want to be seen at the game; they’re not necessarily fans,” Kolek said. “Maybe Taylor Swift. I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” However, he backtracked slightly after making his remarks. He admitted that she might have “a lot going on so she can’t come all the time.” Ultimately, he found her appearance at Game 4 of the NBA Finals to be “a little performative.” Naturally, this was a controversial take, given Swift’s hardcore Swiftie fan base. She attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals with Este and Alana Haim and Mariska Hargitay. They were some of the team’s loudest supporters during their thrilling comeback. item.title: Where the Yankees' bullpen stands and what's next after latest addition
item.description: Rebuilding the Yankees' bullpen was an early offseason priority for GM Brian Cashman. On Monday, the Yanks agreed with veteran lefty Brent Suter on a one-year contract, as first reported by ESPN's Jeff Passan. Suter, 37, an 11-year MLB veteran, split time last season with the Los Angeles Angels and Atlanta Braves, posting a 3.36 ERA (122 ERA-plus) in 54 appearances, covering 91 innings. Earlier this month, closer David Bednar accepted the $23.15 million free agent qualifying offer, securing his services for 2027. Veteran lefty Tim Hill was re-signed and the Yanks reunited with right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga on a two-year deal, after his successful 2026 season with the Arizona Diamondbacks . Right-handers Fernando Cruz and Luis Gil were non-tendered last week, saving roughly $4.6 million in estimated 2027 salary. The expensive reunion with Bednar and the signing of Loaisiga (set to earn $18 million through 2028) and Suter (guaranteed $4 million, with an option for 2028) might be the extent of the Yanks' heavy pursuit of relievers this winter. Top free agent lefty Adrian Morejon has the Yanks' interest, but he could command a lucrative multi-year deal, while free agent righty Paul Blackburn could net a similar contract as Loaisiga received. And the Yanks have further business to address - before or after the anticipated Dec. 1 MLB lockout - including ways to upgrade or boost depth at catcher, the infield and center field. Moving third baseman Ryan McMahon's remaining $16 million contract for 2027 and exploring potential deals for Luis Garcia Jr., Ryan Weathers and the Yanks' pitching surplus are also up for discussion. Suter gives the Yankees three lefties in their 2027 bullpen, along with Hill and Brent Headrick, a converted starter who had a breakout 2026 season but tired down the stretch. The soft-tossing Suter brings a wealth of bullpen experience and a knack for inducing soft contact and groundballs, which he did at a roughly 50-percent clip in 2026, per MLB Statcast. Armed with a sinker-changeup-fastball-slider mix, Suter has generally produced neutral splits; he was better against righty hitters in '26, limiting them to a .651 OPS versus .772 against lefty hitters. A 31st-round draft pick by the Milwaukee Brewers in 2012, Suter is a Harvard graduate who received his degree in environmental science and public policy. item.title: Jeffery Simmons Sends Playful Warning To Tom Brady After Bears Win
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears kept their winning streak alive by beating the New Orleans Saints 21-13 on Sunday. This is the team’s fifth straight victory. Following the final whistle, defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons took time to speak with reporters on the field. He did not hold back when asked about the upcoming game against the Detroit Lions and the legendary quarterback watching from the booth. A Message for the Legend Simmons knows the buzz around Tom Brady is real, but he wants the Bears to stay focused on the job at hand. The defensive star told Fox Sports that the opponent in the booth changes nothing about their mindset. “It really don’t matter if it’s Detroit, Tom Brady — we’re still playing,” Simmons said. He made it clear that respect for Brady does not mean fear of the matchup. “No offense, much respect. The greatest quarterback to play this game, but it doesn’t matter who lines up across from us. Our job is to go out there and dominate,” he added. Simmons has faced Brady before during his time with the Tennessee Titans. When asked if he ever managed to sack the future Hall of Famer, Simmons laughed and admitted he could not recall a specific moment. Despite the lack of a sack, he noted that he did have a role in ending Brady’s season in New England. “I ended up putting him out of the playoffs his last year in New England, though, so that felt good,” he said. He also shared that former Titans coach Mike Vrabel has nothing but good things to say about the quarterback. Locker Room Bonds The playful tone Simmons showed on the field matches the energy inside the Bears’ locker room. Teammates are not afraid to mess with the defensive tackle during practice drills. Sports Mockery reported a specific incident involving defensive lineman Daniel Hardy. During a drill, the group had to tip the ball while a teammate tried to catch it. Hardy, knowing Simmons was standing behind him, decided to tip the ball far off course. Simmons had to scramble to catch the ball before it hit the turf. The defensive tackle showed his reaction with a single-finger salute afterward. Simmons believes Hardy did it on purpose to get a reaction. Hardy, however, maintains that the throw was wide and the whole thing was unintentional. This banter shows the team is comfortable with each other even as they fight for wins. Looking Ahead to Detroit The Bears will carry this momentum into their next game on the road. The team faces a tough test when they travel to Ford Field to play the Detroit Lions. This matchup will happen on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET. The Bears, coming off five straight wins, face the Lions.

item.title: Americas Football Round Up: Boca Juniors Crowned Copa Sudamericana Champions
item.description: This weekend had some monumental results across the Americas for football in 2026. The biggest headlines? Another international title for the famous Boca Juniors of Argentina, while the MLS and Liga MX playoffs took steps forward. Here is your recap of all the action. Boca Juniors Wins Copa Sudamericana Boca Juniors dominated the final of the 2026 Copa Sudamericana, emerging as 2-0 winners over Atletico Mineiro of Brazil. Santiago Ascacibar had the opener, and Miguel Merentiel had the dagger in the 48th minute as Boca won their third ever Sudamericana title, and their first since 2005. Boca had not won an international title in nearly two decades. Played in Colombia, Colombia’s own Sebastian Villa also contributed to the Boca victory, while Colombian international Alvaro Montero kept a clean sheet in goal, as they now chase another Argentine league title to close the season. Mineiro delivered a toothless performance as their focus now turns to the table finish in the Brasileiro. A match that was played in brutal heat and humidity, Boca’s leader, Argentine midfielder Leandro Paredes fainted post match during an interview with DSports the broadcaster. Flamengo Crowned Champions in Brazil Facing their direct rivals for the title Palmeiras, at the Palmeiras stadium, Flamengo did what they needed to do to win the 2026 Brazilian league title, a 1-1 draw with Palmeiras. Samuel Lino equalized the match in the 76th minute, to give Flamengo their 10th title. Palmeiras late season slump knocking them out of the title hunt before the season concludes. In an Easter Egg moment against a rival, Flamengo celebrated with the trophy in Palmeiras stadium, despite the CBF trying to prevent it, the 2025 League Champions Trophy was snuck into the stadium in an equipment bag, producing an iconic post-match scene. Flamengo, Palmeiras, and likely Cruzeiro have already punched their tickets to next year’s Copa Libertadores, and Palmeiras plays the Copa Libertadores 2026 final on Saturday against Estudiantes, meaning they can’t sulk from this draw for long. What hangs over the Brasileiro for 2027 and beyond is Brazil’s ban on sports betting and related advertising that is set to impact clubs financially. As for the rest of this season? Internacional, Gremio, and Corinthians are hovering on the relegation bubble, with Remo and Chapecoense already facing a grim fate. Sao Paulo and Botafogo are among the teams battling for a place in South American tournament football. Liga MX’s Liguilla is Set Monterrey’s 2-0 win over Pumas, via a brace from Argentine Luca Orellano that included a “bend it like Beckham” style goal from distance, was enough to secure their play in the final eight for the Liga MX playoffs to conclude 2026. Pumas were eliminated by other results around the league, and Monterrey were the team that survived despite playing with 10 men. Orellano is a talented player but he had adopted a bench role under Matias Almeyda, only to finish the regular season as a hero.

It's still keeping the focus on one game at a time because that's the only thing you can control. It's going out preparing your best throughout the week and handling the game the proper way by executing, finishing the right way. Then you go on to the next one.” Q: On the Baltimore Ravens without QB Lamar Jackson Ryans: “The Ravens still, even without Lamar, the run game is the most important thing. item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer reacts during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Shane Beamer entered the 2026 college football season knowing there was pressure to turn things around at South Carolina. After a disappointing 4-8 campaign in 2025, expectations were high for the Gamecocks to bounce back and compete in the SEC. However, another season filled with frustrating losses and inconsistent performances has put Beamer’s future in Columbia under the microscope once again. The pressure surrounding Beamer started building early in the season. South Carolina suffered several difficult losses, including blown leads against Mississippi State and Kentucky. Those performances raised serious questions about the team’s ability to finish games and whether Beamer could get the program moving in the right direction. The Gamecocks’ 49-18 loss to Alabama was another major setback. South Carolina struggled on both sides of the football, and the defeat added to the growing frustration among the fanbase. Following the loss, reports indicated that Beamer’s job security was becoming a major conversation within the program. A Late Season Collapse Raises More Questions For a while, it appeared Beamer had managed to quiet some of the criticism. South Carolina responded to its early struggles by winning four consecutive games, improving to 6-3 and climbing to No. 17 in the national rankings. However, the momentum quickly disappeared. The Gamecocks suffered a stunning 34-6 loss to Arkansas before returning home to face No. 1 Georgia. South Carolina struggled to generate offense in both contests, losing consecutive games by identical scores. The loss to Georgia was particularly frustrating because the Gamecocks entered halftime trailing just 10-6. However, the Bulldogs dominated the second half, scoring 24 unanswered points to secure the victory. South Carolina finished with just 218 total yards, while quarterback LaNorris Sellers struggled to find consistency against Georgia’s defense. The back to back performances have brought the hot seat conversation back into the spotlight. item.title: Davis Love III Defends Fanless RSM Finish After Weather Chaos
item.description: Davis Love III putts on eight during the first round of the U.S. Senior Open at Scioto Country Club in Columbus on July 2, 2026. Fans will not be present to view the final round as the PGA Tour season concludes. Davis Love III defended this controversial call after severe rain wiped out Saturday play at the RSM Classic. The tournament moved the decisive round to Monday, but the host said crowds cannot return due to a total loss of volunteer staff and security assets. Love admitted the scale of the storm caught everyone off guard. Speaking on Golf Channel during Sunday’s action, the Hall of Famer said, “We weren’t really prepared.” He noted that even the official Tour meteorologist on site did not expect such heavy rain. “Even our meteorologist on site from the Tour, they were surprised at what we got,” Love said. The downpour waterlogged the Seaside Course in Georgia, forcing officials to delay play multiple times until golf became impossible. Why Monday Crowds Are Impossible The logistics of a working Monday simply do not support a large fan base after such a disruption. Love stated that holding the final round before spectators on a working Monday is logistically unfeasible because vital infrastructure and manpower have been lost. The tournament lost access to its parking areas and, more critically, its 1,200 volunteers. “Parking, mainly our 1,200 volunteers. That’s the biggest thing,” he told GolfMagic . Without these people, the event cannot handle security, buses, or food services safely. Love emphasized that the players must still play to determine the winner and secure next year’s cards. “We’ve got guys playing not only to win a golf tournament but trying to improve their position and get a card for next year, and we can’t have fans because we’ve lost so many assets for tomorrow,” he added. A Season Ending in Silence This weather event has stripped the traditional Sunday atmosphere from the season’s conclusion. Despite MacCurrach Golf and Sea Island grounds staff executing an unbelievable job to drain the bunkers, the human element remains absent. Love acknowledged the trade-off, stating, “So we’re going to be able to get the players out to play, and that’s the main thing, give them a good golf course. Obviously they won’t hear quite as much cheering.” The players will finish the tournament in near silence. Refunds and exchanges for tickets purchased for Saturday remain subject to existing policies, meaning fans who paid for the washed-out action may not see the final round they bought. The weather disrupted the small tournament, which has limited resources. Love praised the bunkers for holding up well despite the rain events since they were built. “The bunkers performed very well,” he said. “MacCurrach Golf, the builder, did an unbelievable job building the bunkers, and we’ve had a lot of rain events since they were built and they held up really well.”

item.title: Mike McCarthy Shuts Down Idea Of QB Change For Steelers: 'Aaron Rodgers Is Our Quarterback'
item.description: Mike McCarthy Shuts Down Idea Of QB Change For Steelers: 'Aaron Rodgers Is Our Quarterback' originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In the grand scheme of things, Aaron Rodgers' age-42 season in the NFL has been solid. Despite being the oldest player in the league, Rodgers was effective enough to lead Pittsburgh to a 6-2 start to the season behind an improved run game. But after a tough two-game stretch, he's on track to total a lower QBR (86.6) and completion percentage (60.9%) with more interceptions (6) and sacks taken (31) than in his 2025 season. Pittsburgh's offense managed just 18 points against Cincinnati, then 16 points against Philadelphia, during a two-game losing streak. But Mike McCarthy made it clear on Monday: Rodgers won't see the bench anytime soon. Here's what McCarthy said about the potential for a quarterback change for the Steelers . MORE: Why DK Metcalf Won't Be Suspended By NFL After Ejection in Loss vs. Eagles Mike McCarthy Shuts Down Idea Of QB Change For Steelers Rodgers has had some strong performances this season, including a three-touchdown day against the Colts and a 292-yard outing in a win over the Bengals. But over the last two losses, he's taken eight total sacks with a completion percentage of 61.6%, generating far less scoring for Pittsburgh. Against the Eagles on Sunday, Rodgers averaged just 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half, which was the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since 2006, per ESPN. Aaron Rodgers averaged just 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half. 🫣 That's the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking in 2006. 12 of his 20 attempts were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage. https://t.co/pocXNeAPrr — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 22, 2026 Part of the reason for the offensive struggles is a decline in run-game production and separation from wide receivers, but Rodgers hasn't elevated the offense much, either. On Monday, ESPN's Brooke Pryor asked McCarthy whether he would consider putting in Mason Rudolph when Rodgers and the offense are struggling, but he shut it down. "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," McCarthy said, per Pryor. While this may be Rodgers' last NFL season, it doesn't appear the Steelers will be giving Rudolph, Will Howard or Drew Allar any starting reps anytime soon. item.title: Padres expected to make big push for Michael King and three other additions
item.description: Padres expected to make big push for Michael King and three other additions originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . During the 2026-2027 MLB offseason, the San Diego Padres have a very clear goal: add to their starting rotation. Signing someone like Tarik Skubal, while an ideal scenario, was not realistic with the ridiculous $450 million winning bid from the New York Mets . Instead, the Padres are going to shop in the next tier down. But that tier includes Michael King, a fan-favorite starter who's a free agent and is sure to land a strong deal this offseason. But will it be with the Padres? MLB insider Bob Nightengale of USA Today is reporting that the Padres are going to make a strong push to bring King back, while also looking to make two other starting pitching additions, on top of potentially bringing Adrian Morejon back. Padres expected to pursue 4 big pitching additions this offseason "They will now do everything possible to bring back Michael King, at least two other starters, with perhaps left-handed reliever extraordinaire Morejon, too," Nightengale writes. San Diego's new ownership group will likely want to get the fanbase on their side, and to do so, making some moves this offseason to upgrade the team is needed. Re-signing King makes the most sense, as he's coming off a great 2026 season, one where he showed some incredible guts in the playoffs. But even if they add King, the Padres are still going to be on the lookout for two more starting pitchers this offseason, according to Nightengale. MORE : Padres interested in re-signing 2.86 ERA starter despite $32M contract decision That makes sense, as the Padres have King, Nick Pivetta, Casey Mize, and Robbie Ray all hitting free agency at the same time this offseason. Bringing Pivetta back would make a ton of sense, as would a deal to bring King back. But the Padres will be on the hunt for another starter, and likely a reliever as well. It's going to cost a fortune to bring back Morejon and King, while adding two good starting pitchers. To compete with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers , they're going to need a lot of help. While it's hard to tell what exactly the Padres will do, based on their strong need in the rotation, it would be a surprise if they didn't make a few roster moves at the MLB level in their starting rotation at some point this offseason, with King the obvious top choice. item.title: How is ex-Packers QB Kyle McCord is playing in place of Malik Willis?
item.description: Kyle McCord had a breakout preseason for the Green Bay Packers . It caught the attention of the Miami Dolphins, who traded for McCord at the end of training camp so he could be their backup quarterback behind former Packers QB Malik Willis. Now, he's getting a chance to start for the Dolphins. Though it's been a small sample size, starting in the regular season is proving to be much more of a challenge than those preseason games. Filling in the last two games for an injured Willis , McCord has completed only 44.6% of his passes, hasn't thrown a touchdown pass and is averaging only 4.8 yards per completion. Their 26-9 loss to the Super Bowl-contending Buffalo Bills on the road Nov. 22 was especially rough for McCord and the Dolphins. They had a season-low 185 yards of total offense and didn't find the end zone. McCord's 32.4 quarterback rating was the lowest of any quarterback in the NFL in Week 10. His 102 passing yards and 36.4 completion percentage – though his receivers had multiple drops – is also the lowest of all starting QBs. The Dolphins, who come to Lambeau Field to play the Packers on Dec. 20, dropped to 1-9. Buy Packers tickets on StubHub Malik Willis injury update McCord will have at least two more weeks as the starting quarterback, with Willis on injured reserve. Willis, the Dolphins' prized free-agent acquisition in the offseason, is battling a groin and core muscle injury. He went on IR in the days after the team's 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions on Nov. 8. While he initially didn't rule out surgery for Willis earlier this month, coach Jeff Hafley said rest was the best way to heal the injury. During a Nov. 23 news conference, Hafley said Willis "doesn’t need the surgery right now." "I don’t foresee him needing the surgery leading up to that time," Hafley said, regarding Willis' four-week IR period. "Once we get to the four weeks, we’ll re-evaluate that to see how he feels and if he’s ready to go. "But, as of today, I would not say, yeah, he’ll have the surgery before that time period." item.title: Ange Postecoglou snaps at reporter over Sadio Mané absence after Al-Nassr loss
item.description: Ange Postecoglou press conference -Credit:Thmanyah Sports Ange Postecoglou confronted a journalist after they challenged him on why Sadio Mané was absent from Al-Nassr's match for the birth of his second child. The former Liverpool forward missed the fixture as his teammates fell 3-1 to Al-Ahli away in the Saudi Pro League. Cristiano Ronaldo had put Al-Nassr ahead early before squandering a penalty. Al-Ahli took advantage and mounted a turnaround, with England international Ivan Toney on the scoresheet. Following the game, a reporter questioned Postecoglou about whether Mané's choice to stay with his wife, Aisha Tamba, demonstrated insufficient dedication to the team. "Are you a father? Do you have children?" the former Tottenham Hotspur manager fired back, via The Mirror . Mauricio Pochettino scraps Man Utd rule after Liverpool loss as players face wake-up call Thomas Müller calls out ‘laissez-faire’ MLS format as Germany legend debates lack of relegation Sadio Mane's marriage to Aisha Tamba shocked the football world -Credit:magvision_evens_officiel/Instagram When the journalist answered 'no', Postecoglou responded: "That's probably why you ask the question. Because when you do, you'll realize it's the most important thing, the biggest blessing you can have. "[Mané] is with his wife while she is having a baby, okay? Nothing is more important in life. Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mané is one of the best people in this world, mate. Never question him or his commitment to this football club." Postecoglou has built a reputation for heated or tense exchanges with the media, particularly during his Premier League tenure. The 61-year-old frequently engaged in uncomfortable discussions with reporters while managing Tottenham and briefly Nottingham Forest. Following Al-Nassr's 4-0 defeat to Al-Ain in the Asian Champions League last September, Postecoglou responded to a reporter who had suggested Ronaldo had done 'nothing' in the match: "You're watching a different game to me." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Friday's defeat marked just Al-Nassr's third loss since Postecoglou assumed control during the summer. However, they sit third in the standings, trailing Al-Hilal by two points, with their rivals holding a game in hand. Mané has netted three goals and registered eight assists across 15 appearances this campaign. The winger arrived at Al-Nassr in summer 2023 after a single season with Bayern Munich. This followed six trophy-laden seasons at Anfield, where he helped Liverpool secure both the Premier League title and Champions League glory. Mané first made his mark in English soccer during two seasons with Southampton. Off the field, Mané married Tamba in 2024. The pair, supported by Mané's substantial £650,000 (just under $847,200) weekly salary, welcomed a daughter last year.

item.title: Maui Invitational: Ole Miss tames Tigers, 82-62
item.description: LAHAINA, HAWAII - NOVEMBER 26: The Southwest Maui Invitational logo is shown on the floor before the championship of the Southwest Maui Invitational between the Southern California Trojans and the Arizona State Sun Devils at the Lahaina Center on November 26, 2025 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Monday morning in Maui was a wire to wire win for the Ole Miss Rebels over the Clemson Tigers, 82-62, in the first game of the Maui Invitational. Ole Miss (5-0) opened things up in dominant fashion going up 20-2 in the early minutes of the game and led by as many as 28 during the game. Clemson (4-2) turned the ball over seven times in the first seven minutes to dig a hole it could come back from, and the Rebels will now move on to play the winner of No. 19 BYU and Washington. This game looked over by halftime with Ole Miss up 50-26, and the two teams traded shots in the second half with neither making any big runs. Truly one of the more complete basketball games Ole Miss has played in the last 12 months. Five Rebels scored in double digits led by Corey Stephenson with 17 points. Ben Henshall came off the bench to score 15 points while guards Ilias Kamardine and Budd Clark each had 13 points. Ole Miss shot 54 percent from the floor and 42 percent from behind the arc while also logging 14 steals and winning the rebound and turnover margin. It’s likely Ole Miss will face BYU next as one of the two favorites to win the Maui Invitational. That game will take place tomorrow, Nov. 24 at 1:30 p.m. CT and will be broadcast on ESPN2.

item.title: Bears-Lions Thanksgiving Clash Sets NFC North Stage
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions both stand at 8-2 heading into their Thanksgiving Day matchup. This game will decide who holds the top spot in the NFC North heading into Week 13. Both teams won their last games to reach this record. On Sunday, the New Orleans Saints fell 21-13 to the Bears as the Lions took down the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21. The winner of this contest will claim sole possession of first place. Chicago improved to 8-2 after a strong defensive showing at Soldier Field. Quarterback Caleb Williams threw two touchdown passes in the victory. Detroit won, holding the Buccaneers to under 275 yards of total offense. It was the fourth straight game in which the Lions’ defense kept opponents under that mark. Division Race Comes Down to One Game The Lions currently sit in first place because they own the tie-breaker. Following wins against the Packers and Vikings, Detroit stands at 2-0 within the NFC North. Chicago is 0-2 in the division due to losses against Minnesota and Green Bay. If the Bears lose on Thursday, they could drop to third place if the Vikings win. The Vikings hold the head-to-head tie-breaker over Chicago from their Week 2 victory. Detroit cannot fall below second place even if they lose. They already beat Minnesota earlier in the season. The Packers remain in last place no matter what happens in the other games. Defensive Stars Lead the Charge Austin Booker picked up a fumble while rookie safety Dillon Thieneman snagged an interception. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons delivered three sacks in the game. He has now tallied five sacks in just three games since joining the team. Simmons matched his career high when he tackled Saints quarterback Tyler Shough late in the fourth quarter. Lions coach Dan Campbell expressed his excitement for the upcoming matchup. Chicago coach Ben Johnson praised his own unit after the Saints game. He added, “I thought those guys played their tails off really for the whole 60 minutes. A ton of sacks throughout. Multiple turnovers that turned into points for us.” Key Stats and Trade Impact The Bears made a bold move to acquire Simmons from Tennessee. Chicago sent three draft picks, including two first-round selections, for the defensive tackle and a fifth-round pick on Oct. 29. Simmons knows what the team expects from him. “I know this team brought me in here and they expect me to win my one-on-ones and I expect to take full advantage of them,” Simmons said. New Orleans coach Kellen Moore admitted his team missed chances to score. “That game wasn’t without the opportunities to make some plays, and we just didn’t get it done,” Moore said. The Saints only scored one touchdown on seven drives that reached Chicago territory. The Bears opened a 10-0 lead with a shovel pass to D’Andre Swift for a three-yard touchdown. The game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Thursday at Ford Field.

item.title: De Bruyne still 'loves' Man City owners despite financial charges
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne became one of Manchester City's all-time greats in a 10-year spell at the club (Paul ELLIS) Kevin De Bruyne said on Monday his love for Manchester City's leadership has not been tainted by a guilty verdict on breaking financial rules, that could tarnish his legacy at the English giants. Napoli playmaker De Bruyne returns to the Etihad Stadium in Champions League action on Tuesday, just over a year since his decade in Manchester came to an end. De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and the Champions League during a golden era for City to become one of the club's all-time greats. However, some of those titles could be stripped unless City successfully overturn a ruling that found them guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules between 2009 and 2018. "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club. I love the owners," De Bruyne told reporters. "I've even spoken to (chairman) Khaldoon (Al Mubarak) about how to buy a club. "I have nothing but affection for this club and that will never change, (the way) the people treated me and my family for 10 years." The Belgian also dismissed suggestions his achievements on the field are now tainted in light of City's financial impropriety. "In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit," he said. "I played in between the white lines. I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most." Napoli are in danger of an early Champions League exit after losing three of their opening four European games of the season. The Italians sit 27th in the 36-team table with only the top 24 progressing. City's form in the Premier League has slumped since their future in the English top-flight was plunged into doubt by the guilty verdict. A severe points deduction and possibly even relegation from the Premier League is expected if City's appeal is not upheld. But Enzo Maresca's men have won three of their four Champions League games to occupy a place in the top eight, who progress directly to the last 16. kca/iwd

item.title: NASCAR Finally Gives Fans The Horsepower Increase They Demanded
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR is finally listening to the fans who have begged for more speed. Beginning in 2027, the sanctioning body declared on Friday that horsepower will increase from 670 to 750 at intermediate-sized tracks. This change kicks off with the Coca-Cola 600 in May and affects major venues like Las Vegas, Kansas, and Michigan. The move addresses years of complaints about cars that were too slow to pass each other on these long ovals. At North Wilkesboro Speedway on May 23, the All-Star Race will see horsepower jump even higher to 800. This specific event will serve as a test bed. If the data looks good, NASCAR and engine builders could roll out this 800-horsepower package for all short tracks and road courses by mid-August at Bristol Motor Speedway. Speed Limits and New Rules NASCAR is also tweaking how drivers are penalized for going too low on the track. After a messy finish at Talladega last month, the rule book needed clarity. The new definition states that driving below the double-yellow line means a car’s left-side tires are “beneath the left line of the inside double-painted lines that separate the apron from the racing surface.” This removes the guesswork for drivers and officials alike. Superspeedways are getting their own adjustments for qualifying. Drivers will now have just one lap to set their time, ditching the old two-round format. Smaller spoilers and increased horsepower within the 510 to 530 range will also be featured during these sessions. NASCAR says these tweaks could push qualifying speeds past 200 mph. However, the race day rules at Daytona and Talladega will stay mostly the same as they were in 2026. Kevin Harvick has commented on the 2027 Clash setup modifications, noting NASCAR might eliminate the rear spoiler’s Lexan extension. Teams will also see the removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season. The removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season is expected to make the car react differently to various setups, forcing crews to find new ways to gain an edge. Rain rules are also shifting, as owner points will now decide the starting grid if qualifying gets washed out. The league is confident in its officials despite past controversies. A NASCAR executive stated, according to the Daily Downforce , “The Officiating Crew Is as Good as It Has Ever Been.” This comes as the sport removes minimum damper length rules to give teams more setup options.

item.title: Serie A | Monza 3-0 Fiorentina: Viola misery as Varela hits 11 in 11
item.description: Serie A | Monza 3-0 Fiorentina: Viola misery as Varela hits 11 in 11 Gustavo Varla is now up to 11 goals from his first 11 appearances in Serie A after netting a brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina on Monday evening, which has seen the Biancorossi leapfrog their opponents in the Serie A table. Goals from Varela (x2) and Jay Robinson handed Monza a much-needed three points in their Serie A match at home against Fiorentina on Sunday night, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone and into 14th place. MONZA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 23: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal from the penalty spot during the Serie A match between AC Monza and ACF Fiorentina at U-Power Stadium on November 23, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Fiorentina had begun the evening in 14th, but have dropped down to 16th as a result of tonight’s game, just one point above the drop zone after 12 matches. Click here to see how today’s teams lined up. Fiorentina were presented with the first real goalscoring opportunity after six minutes: Monza goalkeeper Demba Thiam, starting ahead of Noel Tornqvist, was off his line and managed to pass the ball straight to Christ Inaou Oulai under little pressure. Thiam was able to recover and make the save after the Ivorian’s weak shot at an empty net. It was Monza who took the lead right at the end of the first half, though: Varela earning and converting a penalty kick just before stoppage time. MONZA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 23: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza scores his team’s first goal from the penalty spot during the Serie A match between AC Monza and ACF Fiorentina at U-Power Stadium on November 23, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Portugal international had lined up a shot in a congested Fiorentina penalty area, which came off the arm of a flailing Oulai. The in-form Varela stepped up and converted into the right-hand side of the net, sending David De Gea the wrong way in the process. Varela’s second goal of the game came shortly after the re-start of the second half. Jay Robinson did well to shrug off Alex Jimenez before sending Matteo Pessina on the run down the left flank. Varela burst into the area and applied a smart, back-heel finish to convert Pessina’s low ball into the six-yard box for 2-0. Robinson made it three less than 10 minutes later. Samuele Birindelli’s cross into the area was headed half-clear, but only as far as the Englishman on the edge of the area, who slammed a volley into the roof of the net with the help of a deflection on its way in. MONZA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 23: Jay Robinson of AC Monza scores his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and ACF Fiorentina at U-Power Stadium on November 23, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Monza now find themselves in 14th place in the Serie A table, whilst Fiorentina have dropped down to 16th, one point above the relegation spot

item.title: Vikings most to blame for Sunday Night Football disaster vs. 49ers in Mexico City
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Vikings most to blame for Sunday Night Football disaster vs. 49ers in Mexico City appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings did not deliver on Sunday Night Football in Week 11. San Francisco blew out Minnesota in a 35-10 beatdown that felt decided before the second half was over. On paper, this game should have been a highly competitive matchup and a potential NFC playoff preview. But it quickly turned into a one-sided blowout. Minnesota boasts arguably the NFL’s best defense and San Francisco has been rolling over almost every team they face. Unfortunately, the Vikings failed in almost every single phase and looked completely outmatched in this international showdown. So what went wrong in this one? And should Vikings fans start being worried about the team’s playoff chances? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Here are the Vikings most to blame for Sunday’s disastrous loss against the 49ers in Mexico City. Is the magic of the Kirk Cousins reunion already over? Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports. Vikings fans were rightfully excited after Cousins won his first game back in a purple uniform. But is the magic already gone? Cousins finished the game 26-of-38 for 235 passing yards and an interception. That lone interception was the turning point in the entire contest. Cousins threw a brutal pick-six just before halftime that gave San Francisco an almost insurmountable 18-point lead. The Vikings were already down 21-10 and attempted a two-minute drill that could’ve made the game competitive. In fact, a touchdown would have sent Minnesota into halftime down just 21-17. The veteran quarterback explained what went wrong on that consequential play after the game. “The backside safety made a great play,” Cousins said. “I need to feel him and progress, and not try to fit it in there.” It is important to remember that Minnesota received the ball first in the second half. Narrowing the margin to just one score would have given the Vikings an opportunity to take the lead with another touchdowns. Admittedly that is a lot of ifs and hypotheticals. But the larger point is that Minnesota was still alive at that point and could have easily turned things around with the proper execution. Instead, Cousins threw the entire game away and the Vikings never scored another point. Perhaps the most troubling aspect here is that the Vikings didn’t appear to have many answers after falling behind. That does not bode well for Cousins and company if they were to make it to the playoffs. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
